reporting-org.narrative: Ethiopian Women with Disabilities National Assocation

title.narrative: AWESOME (Advancing Women's Engagement Strengthening opportunities to mobilize for Equality

description.narrative: A 5 year advocacy programme to support women’s movements in Ethiopia, Kenya and Uganda to be strengthened, less fragmented and more representative of diverse groups of women, including women with disabilities. These stronger women’s movements will contribute to strong women leaders at all levels, and the prevention and elimination of sexual and gender based violence (SGBV) against women and girls.

title.narrative: An increase in gender sensitive and disability inclusive coverage and reporting in the media
Number of media spots that promote women’s (including WwDs) rights related to SGBV (sub-national level)

description.narrative: Society 2.5: Number of radio shows played (140 focused on disability inclusion in women's participation and leadership on 8 March International Women's Day; and 140 shows will be SGBV focused and played during 16 Days of Activism).

comment.narrative: Although media is a powerful tool to bring behavioral change, and media can strengthen the voices of diverse women to champion a new narrative around gender equality, 41% of baseline respondents believe that their issue is not addressed by the media. Baseline value is 0 because no AWESOME media has been created yet.

In Years 3-5, 136 media spots were broadcast (83 related to SGBV and 53 related to women’s participation and leadership). In year 5, 52 radio programs were broadcast with an estimated audience reached of 20-25 million Ethiopians, representing a huge audience for these civil society messages about women and WWDs’ rights. One program focused on the achievements of AWESOME in the past 4 and half year with respect to increasing participation. EWDNA members, families, community leaders and government stakeholders were interviewed on what AWESOME has achieved so far. Other topics include GBV, workplace harassment and ratification of ILO C190, election participation of WWDs, participation in the national dialogue process.This indicator also captured 4 TV shows. For example, one show in Year 4 was about participation of WWDs in the transitional justice process.Different feedbacks coming at the end of the radio shows showed the lack of disability friendly services, absence of enabling environment for effective participation of WWDs, the invisibility of empowered WWDs in public spheres, the attention to be given for WWDs vulnerability to GBV and the related poor service to access justice. In terms of creating space for WWDs' voices, EWDNA has observed that more media coverage is given for issues disability specially around international day of PWDs. EWDNA observed increased disability awareness and better understanding around disability and increase community life participation of WWDs. The radio program has increased understanding of Disability, participation, GBV by the wider public as per the feedbacks received from audiences.

This is 29 in Year 1 (28 sub-national and 1 national) and 7 in Year 2 (1 sub national and 4 national). In year 1, 56 radio programs in 2 local language have been organized (sub-national level). One TV advertisemnt is aired on Major media outlet for 10 days and one TV talkshow have been organized. * Activity 4.2: As per the plan of producing media spots on the local Bisrat FM radio stations twice per year, using International women’s day (March 8) 28 programs and International Day of Persons with Disabilities (Dec 3) 28 programs a four weeks radio program on the inclusion challenges of women with disabilities in election and political participation have been conducted on local FM radio stations using the local languages of Amharic and Gammo(widely spoken language in southern Ethiopia). According to the media assessment carried every 6 month, the radio station has 4.5 million audiences. The Amahric version of this year’s March 8 celebration motto focuses on using our voice for decisions that matter in our life. Particularly in this case , the 6th national election of Ethiopia. It focuses primarily on encouraging WWDs to go out and use their voice there by show how polling centres are inaccessible for PWDAll the 56 radio programs were sub national level. It reach South Ethiopia Gammo speaking people and Addis Abeba with 125KM radius area coverage with Amharic language which is the widely spoken language in the country. * Activity 4.3: Two TV programs were prepared by EWDNA. One of them is a 1 minute spot(advertisement) on how basic services like schools, clinics and transport are inaccessible for girls and women with disabilities both physically and in terms of communication barriers for deaf people. The spot was aired at prime time in Ethiopian broadcast Corporation (the main news outlet of government media). The spot lasted 10 days on air. The other is a Sunday entrainment program on EBS Tv( Is based in Ethiopia with correspondents both in United States at its headquarters in Silver Spring, Maryland, U.S) where EWDNA’s Executive Director Dibabe Bacha, used a program named “coffee time” where it has a larger viewer on Sunday to talk about women and girls with disabilities. Both TV programs have a international and national level coverage with the largest viewer in the country. Success: These two media spots has increased notion of disability inclusion and boosted EWDNA’s visibility. In year 2: EWDNA received data on the number of listeners - according to the media assessment 4.5 million people listen the local radio and 85 % of Ethiopian population listens the national radio program. After the stories were heard, calls and feedbacks were received from the public that, the vulnerability of WWDs is understood and many are shocked on how the justice system failed to serve justice to those women. Through this media, this was an opportunity for WWD to talk about their experiences and challenge stereotypes/norms surrounding WWDs. The radio program creates an opportunity for the larger public, CSO and government to see the status of WWDs in terms of right protection & promotion, what are the gaps, and what is the role of each stakeholder. More awareness creation opportunities are provided on SGBV as real life stories, the practice of the justice system in responding to GBV survivor WWDs, how the community’s practice holds back women from reporting etc are covered. EWDNA receives phone calls from girls and WWDs who mainly would like to be a member. EWDNA also got feedback from the public in general on appreciating the program, acknowledging that this is the first time to hear about disability and SGBV.The reason for underachievement of target is the high inflation rate in Ethiopia (33%) and as a result hotel service price, fuel, and radio broadcasting service fees has gone up. Inflation has also affected the delivery capacity of the project, especially in conducting the number of radio programs planned in the project, thus to address the challenge EWDNA reduced the number of radio programs. EWDNA shifted unused budget from consultancy budget line to radio programs to maintain the year 3 target of producing 56 radio programs. Targets for Y4 and Y5 will be relooked at and considered in relation to inflation during that time period.

Our target is for the voices of WWds to be included in media programmes. This will be 7 radio programs, played twice a year (on disability and women's international days), across 4 regions. One message that is translated into local languages, and shares the voices of diverse women. The longer-term change we are seeking is that WDROs no longer have to pay for inclusion in media programming voices of WWDs included in media programmes.

title.narrative: Increased collective advocacy efforts by women's rights organisation (WRO) actors for policy change and legal reform, national and regional level
Number of influencing spaces attended or facilitated related to SGBV and participation

description.narrative: Formal institutions 3.5: Number of public events and national and International events held

comment.narrative: EWDNA has been hosting multiple regional events for the past 20 years, but with AWESOME we will focus more on these events at national level meaning participation from different regions of the country, which we see as important to have representation and to make the implementation uniform.

EWDNA organized 3 sub national level events under AWESOME(2 with SWDA and one for presenting legal gap assessment finding) In addition EWDNA was invited in 4 national level events to comment of GBV, Gender policies and also on Disability act.EWDNA organised public events that were very helpful for advocating sub national and national legal gaps for the policy /law making bodies. Especially the sub national level advocacy event was the one the policy gap with respect to disability inclusion presented and reached at consensus of the need for having memorandum of understanding on revision of laws. For example, by partnering with SWDA who have a long time successful presence and acceptance in Oromia region EWDNA can easily sell its disability inclusion agendas to government officials specially justice sector operators. The collaboration will also ease the effort EWDNA is expected to put in getting the attention and action of government bodies. Bu jointly working with SWDA, it was made possible to get the right/targeted government officials both elected women and justice office professionals from Oromia region. Beyond their turnout to our joint trainings their commitment to learn and make changes with respect to disability inclusive GBV response services was impressive.

In Years 3-5, EWDNA held 9 national and 23 sub-national or regional events, contributing to the grand total of 35 events held over the 5 year programme. Events included session with women’s rights organisations (WROs), advocacy workshops, sessions with elected women leaders, policy makers, Ministry of Health, GBV shelters, and with justice sector professionals. Initiatives were implemented as planned and complemented the advocacy efforts of WROs. For example, the year 5 workshop with WROs focused on joining forces to demand changes to the proposed provisions in the drafted CSO law. The draft-imposed restrictions on CSOs from engaging in civic and voter education, which is a key approach to empowering women for political participation and leadership. Through the convening, WROs submitted a letter calling for the removal of these restrictions which is in contradiction with other commitments of the government to empower women, as they would hinder organizations working on women’s participation and leadership; because of this joint action, the government lifted the restriction in the final CSO law. With the justice sector and elected women, EWDNA continues to advocate for disability-sensitive GBV response mechanisms. Based on learning from earlier year events, EWDNA adapted the events to demand concrete changes, ask progress made in their practice, inclusion of disability in their program documents so that we are able to see the changes in awareness being translated into practice.
Of the 9 public events, only 2 are at national level ( 1 in year 4 and 1 in year 5), other are all regional (e.g. one region of Amhara, or SNNPR within Ethiopia) and local level events.

title.narrative: An increase in the number and diversity of women supported with training, awareness raising, and networking
Number of women supported with training, awareness raising, and networking.

description.narrative: Self 1.2: Number of women (yellow movement member university students, WWDs, women participating in the women’s movement) who report feeling their issues and needs have been recognized by the wider group.

comment.narrative: WWDs stated that their issues are not well addressed by the movements. Only 15% of WWDs knew the existence of any active movements for WWDs, gender equality, disability, and SGBV. This indicator is targeting: WROs, Yellow Movement leaders and WWDs through trainings and events. Here youth movement participants are mainly targeted (75%) while WRO leaders (25%) are expected to be welcoming and give recognition to those gender movements in University.
